anchors.caption: Final-protocol medians for six authentic dimension-108 anchor cells (seconds).
anchors.notes: Three warmup rounds and seven timed rounds per cell; each value is a median. All rows cover one selected cell, not a whole root. QUEUE-DENSE is capacity-inapplicable. The 0x2003 K2 median has IQR 91.0567–145.7907 s; that row is retained. A separate later run on the 0x1001 cell (one warmup and three timed rounds per backend, data/hash_join_n108_anchor.csv) gives medians K2 47.9287, K2-WIDE 27.4693 and ARWLF 0.8902 s, and 72.6718 s (11.83 ns per logical pair) for an untuned scalar exact hash join (linear-probing table keyed on the W-bit residual, then a high-bit check; table build included). In every round each backend matches an untimed K2-WIDE reference; the cell has no full-quotient matches, so this checks only for false matches.

aggregates.caption: Geometric-mean speedups on authentic dimension-108 cells, with the final-protocol subset kept separate.
aggregates.notes: Pooled estimates weight cells equally and combine declared discovery/final protocols. Intervals resample entire roots as blocks (10,000 percentile draws, seed 0xB007); only three independent roots occur per role. Equal-root calibration sensitivity gives 52.7449, 32.7335, and 52.0020 for the three ratios; holdout equal-root estimates coincide with pooled estimates. Final anchors have one cell per root.

sparse.caption: Complete authentic dimension-72 prepared-root medians (milliseconds), covering all 4,096 cells.
sparse.notes: Final protocol: three warmup and seven timed rounds. QUEUE-DENSE wins all four rows and the dispatcher runs it in every sample. Regret divides dispatcher median by the fastest legal reporter median, including K2. No end-to-end list-generation cost is included.

positive.caption: Constructed target augmentation on authentic source families of calibration root 0x1001: medians in seconds.
positive.notes: Every case uses one warmup and three timed rounds. Residue-exact counts also equal the attached finite-predicate counts in these records: M for positives and zero for decoys. That predicate has (negative, zero, positive) = (2,86,20), not the production binary-root distribution. Constructed coordinates and residues are assigned separately; original-weight consistency and native L1 membership are unestablished. Only one root has completed repeated evidence.

whole.caption: Complete dimension-108 prepared root 0x1001: every backend over all 4,096 cells (single measured passes).
whole.notes: Each run covers 4,096 cells and 25,189,929,333,072 logical pairs and reports the same single residue-exact EntryId triple (the constructed target). K2 runs family-major as 64 calls, one per target family u, in the order of a single call; its chunks took 2,694 to 4,959 s (median 2,885 s). The dispatcher selected ARWLF in both passes (probes 200 and 176 ms). No warmup or repeated rounds; the K2 run spans daytime machine use, and no interference log was recorded.

scaling_validation.caption: Occupancy model and cross-root checks at the measured dimensions.
rows: Captured mean entries per L1 list
scaling_validation.notes: Sizes use 22 captures of seed 0x7201 and seven captures of seed 0x8001 (attempts 0-6); n108 times use six completed roots (attempts 0-5). Census and survival checks use comparable campaign roots, not those same captures. Poisson means use |L1|/(64*8192); byte widths are 8,8,8,4 at n72 and 8,8,8,8 at n108. Only dense time uses the observed 0.1377 ns/pair coefficient. Zero n72 survivors does not validate the tiny predicted probability.

scaling_n144.caption: Hypothetical dimension-144 geometry retaining thirteen-bit leaves.
scaling_n144.notes: Equation (8) is scaled by the n72 measured/model ratio (0.6123), the n108 ratio (0.8122), or left unscaled. These are scenarios, not confidence bounds. Q=91 and n=144 exceed the frozen key implementation's limits; no n144 backend ran. Storage excludes prepared keys, directories, temporaries and output. The 48-byte record is an n108 proxy; the native snapshot formula gives 68 bytes/entry at n144.

scaling_cost.caption: Conditional cost scenarios for one dimension-144 root.
rows: Fixed geometry, all hardware CPU cores (years)
Pair sweep only, all hardware CPU cores (hours)
scaling_cost.notes: A hypothetical wider-key design retains the observed 0.1377 ns/pair coefficient. Fixed geometry adds a saturated posting scan with coefficient 0.7686 ns inferred from the decoy time contrast. Pair sweep only drops that scan term; the listed retuned geometries were not implemented and their setup, directories, residual recovery and communication are unmodeled. Hardware-core figures divide by 630,784 hypothetical equal-speed CPU cores; Frontier defaults to 551,936 allocatable cores. Intel-to-AMD rate transfer is unmeasured and GPUs are absent. These are conditional model costs, not achieved runtimes or universal lower bounds. List construction adds per attempt; attempt count multiplies the per-attempt sum.

integration.notes: Acceptance uses a binary parent of weight n/2, independently verified against the original balanced modular instance. The benchmark sink's FiniteSanity predicate is absent from this path. All staged solves use the same executables; the forced-ARWLF run was unpinned beside the running n108 solve, so neither run's root times are controlled measurements. Release test evidence comes from a saved development log; the differential ASan result is a recorded rerun (data/asan_differential_record.json). The n108 instance has a planted solution, so exhausting 32 attempts reflects TER's finite per-attempt success probability, not unsatisfiability. Design-B times are the classic solver's level-one-to-root stage time, medians of seven solves after three warmups (ter_full_bench reports medians only); staged times are medians of seven pinned runs after one warmup, cover sink reset and the backend call, and exclude snapshot load and key preparation (32-47 ms per run); design B's stage includes its own setup (about 5 ms). The two stage boundaries differ, so the design-B ratios are approximate. No matched full-solver speedup is reported.

per_root.notes: Each value is a geometric mean over that root's declared cells, mixing the declared discovery and final protocols. With three roots per role, the root-block bootstrap interval of Table 2 equals the range of the three values shown here.

protocols.caption: Measurement protocols and completed case counts, preserving workload and scope boundaries.
protocols.notes: The first eight rows sum to 221 completed regime cases. Nine orphan timings from one interrupted attempt remain outside those complete-case groups. All 10 roots are censused at all 4,096 cells; census is not timing. Cases from one root share an independent input instance. Three unreachable rows are statuses, not omitted failures or timed points.

target_detail.caption: Target-density ablation medians (seconds), with full-density anchor protocol stated explicitly.
target_detail.notes: Source pair mass is fixed within each root. Full-density references use three warmups/seven timed rounds; thinned cases use one/three, seed 0xA11CE001. Target thinning changes occupancy/filter selectivity and posting recovery, while observed packet occupancy L is nearly unchanged. This is a controlled sensitivity study, not an isolated causal instruction-cost decomposition.

crossover_confirm.caption: Final-protocol confirmations of the source-thinning crossover bracket.
crossover_confirm.notes: Three warmups/seven timed rounds, thinning seed 0xA11CE001. Rival = min(K2-WIDE, legal QUEUE-DENSE); QUEUE-DENSE is capacity-inapplicable here. Ratios below one favor ARWLF. The dispatcher runs K2-WIDE in all six cases; it misses the measured ARWLF gain near L=2. The two tested points bracket rather than identify an exact universal threshold.
